p: בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (בְּהַעֲלוֹתְךָ, זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קנב, ב)
In the holy Zohar (Behaaloscha, Zohar III 152b):
"And if you will say that on a higher level
he stands in the second month,
that there would be a special distinction
for one who brings Pesach Sheni in Iyar,
so that it was necessary to say, "it is not so," etc.?
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא (בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ שָׁם)
according to what is brought (in the holy Zohar, ibid.)
Rather, a man who is a man
and is fit to receive a lofty neshamah," etc.
which is the aspect of Keser Elyon.
It is like the infant in its mother's womb,
"And a lamp is lit for him above his head,
from one end of the world to the other."
This is the aspect of the primordial light,
with which Adam HaRishon would gaze
from one end of the world to the other
and He hid it away for the tzaddikim in the time to come;
and it is the aspect of Keser Elyon.
And an infant in its mother's womb
שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ עוֹד שְׁלִיטַת יֵצֶר הָרָע
is one in whom the yetzer hara does not yet hold sway
until he emerges from the womb
from the verse "sin crouches at the door,"
while the neshamah is given into him from the moment of conception
And this is "the lamp of Hashem is the soul of man,"
which was lit above his head;
and he then merits the hidden light
stored for the tzaddikim in the time to come
And it says, "a man who is a man,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
according to what is brought in the holy Zohar
טוֹב אִישׁ דָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא
"'Good is the man' — this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
"and it is written, 'Hashem is a man of war,'" etc.;
דָּבָר אַחֵר טוֹב אִישׁ דָּא צַדִּיק וְכוּלֵּי
"another explanation: 'Good is the man' — this is the tzaddik," etc.;
"Rabbi Chiya said: it is all one."
(and this was explained in Noach, maamar 7).
And "Yaakov and Yosef are as one,
and they have a single image"
(זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א קעו, סוֹף עַמּוּד ב)
this is "the middle bar shall pass through," etc.,
the aspect of the middle line.
עָמְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ זֶה מֹשֶׁה
"They stood still for the sake of a man — this is Moshe,
as it is written, 'And the man Moshe,' etc.;
יָרְדוּ עַל גַּב אִישׁ זֶה יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
they came down for the sake of a man — this is Yehoshua,
as it is written, 'a man in whom there is spirit.'"
That is, Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
was a chariot for the attribute of Ayin,
most hidden of all the hidden, which is called Ayin
וּבְאִדְרָא זוּטָא, חֵלֶק ג רפח, ב)
and in the Idra Zuta, III 288b).
"And Moshe merited them all and took them," etc.
And this is the lamp lit above his head.
on what is derived from the verse,
as it is written, "And Moshe would take the tent,"
from the expression "when His lamp shone above my head"
and he does not bring it from the verse
"Behold, even the moon does not shine,"
and is closer to the word "ohel";
but from the verse "when His lamp shone," etc.,
is derived that "a lamp is lit for him," etc.,
וְזֶהוּ סוֹד מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין לא, ב)
And this is the secret of what Chazal say (Sanhedrin 31b):
"To the one whose radiance is like that of Bisyah's son" —
they ascribed it to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that was lit above his head,
And he is a chariot for the Name Havayah,
like Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
as is brought in the Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 13):
"from the side of the middle pillar," etc.
כָּל שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא שָׁרְשֵׁי נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל
all six hundred thousand roots of the souls of Yisrael.
Yehoshua — "a man in whom there is spirit" —
and they expounded (in the Sifrei, cited by Rashi)
that he could go along with the spirit
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (נְדָרִים כב, ב)
And this accords with what Chazal say (Nedarim 22b):
they would have been given only," etc.,
for it is the setting-out of Eretz Yisrael."
And we explained that "eretz" means the Shechinah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס רמג, ב)
(as brought in the Raaya Mehemna, Pinchas, Zohar III 243b),
וְכָל שֵׁבֶט יֵשׁ לוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה מְיוּחֶדֶת
and each tribe has a distinct holiness
יֵשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
has a portion in Torah she'b'al peh,
and corresponding to it is his portion in the Land.
And upon this was founded the Book of Yehoshua,
which clarifies the root of every tribe
and the root of every Jewish soul
And this is a foretaste of the future,
דִּכְתִיב וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד אִישׁ וְגוֹמֵר
as it is written, "And no longer shall a man teach," etc.,
for then each one will attain
his portion in Torah she'b'al peh.
And this is what is said, "And you shall place of your glory," etc. —
for it is stated in Tosafos (Shabbos 88a)
that they were of hod, of glory;
and this too reaches to the root,
the lamp lit above his head.
And this is what the holy Zohar says,
דְּעַל כֵּן נֶאֱמַר אִישׁ אִישׁ שְׁתֵּי פְּעָמִים
that therefore "ish ish" is said twice:
"rather, a man who is a man
and is fit to receive a lofty neshamah" —
that is, up to the root, from Keser Elyon,
דְּבֶאֱמֶת גַּם עֵשָׂו נִקְרָא אִישׁ אִישׁ
For in truth Esav too is called "ish ish,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא (זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג פט, א)
"for she is not the portion of Esav,
nor was she in the lot of that one
דִּכְתִיב בֵּיהּ אִישׁ יוֹדֵעַ צַיִד אִישׁ שָׂדֶה
of whom it is written, 'a man who knows hunting, a man of the field'" —
because he is from a root
that is the beginning of the kelipah
and the kingship of the kelipah,
as it is said, "Amalek was the first of the nations,
and it is called the wicked kingdom,
and he is in the kelipah down to the root.
And afterward the holy Zohar says:
a man who is fit to be a man
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים צג, א)
And this accords with what Chazal say (Pesachim 93a):
גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר בֵּין שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים וְכוּלֵּי
"A convert who converted between the two Pesachs," etc.;
כָּל שֶׁזָּקוּק לָרִאשׁוֹן זָקוּק לַשֵּׁנִי וְכוּלֵּי
whoever is obligated in the first is obligated in the second," etc.
וּסְבִירָא לֵיהּ לַזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ כְּרַבִּי נָתָן
And the holy Zohar holds like Rabbi Nasan,
and this is what it says:
"a man who is fit to be a man," etc. —
to exclude a convert and a minor,
who were not fit for the Pesach at the first one.
And it says, "and he defiles himself,
so that the holiness from above does not rest upon him" —
the aspect of holiness from above, up to the root;
meaning that they are bound to the supernal root.
And this is why the Pesach
And this is "a man who is a man":
one who was fit for the holiness of the Pesach,
which shows that he is bound to the root,
because a person who defiles himself
But it is written, 'or on a distant road,'
which shows two separate things," etc.;
"here, before he is defiled from above;
here, after he is defiled from above," etc.;
לָא יִשְׁרֵי עֲלֵיהּ קְדוּשָּׁה דִּלְעֵילָּא וְכוּלֵּי
the holiness from above does not rest upon him," etc.
That is, the first Pesach offering in its time
that one is bound to the root, in Keser Elyon,
"If he does not rectify himself, no;
but once he has purified and rectified himself,
there is the second month," etc.;
מִכָּאן כָּל בַּר נָשׁ דִּמְדַכֵּי גַּרְמֵי
"from here: every person who purifies himself
That is, he does teshuvah properly;
and it says that he brings Pesach Sheni —
that is, to exclude the one who says "dezavin"
that on the second they offer it in tumah.
And about this the holy Zohar says:
"And if you will say that on a higher level
he stands in the second month" —
that is, like the one who says (Berachos 34b):
"In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
And about this it says, "it is not so,
who made the Pesach in its time,
took the moon and the sun together" —
that is, on the level of "ish ish":
Moshe and Yehoshua, sun and moon
"The face of Moshe was like the face of the sun;
the face of Yehoshua, like the face of the moon."
And they are a chariot for the Names: Havayah,
Do not say the supernal foundation
of the Tzaddik of the world" —
"the tzaddik is the foundation of the world" —
"rather, the foundation of the precious stone,
And this is the attribute of Malchus,
(בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר סִימָן קצ, נִדְפָּס בְּסוֹף זוֹהַר חֵלֶק א)
(in Sefer HaBahir, siman 190, printed at the end of Zohar I):
the stone that Avraham and Yitzchak rejected,
And David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus.
And this is what it says:
And this is the meaning of what is said in the Gemara
so that Pesach Sheni, which is not sanctified as a festival,
does not require Hallel when it is eaten.
the first is counted in Mitzrayim,
as it is said, "You shall have a song
as on the night when a festival is sanctified."
while it does not write "mekudash lechag,"
is because then Hashem Yisbarach sanctified
the very concept of the holiness of the festival;
that is, then there came into being
the aspect of Malchus, Knesses Yisrael,
when Yisrael accepted His kingship, blessed be He.
And this is what it says:
"who takes the foundation of the precious stone" —
the aspect of Malchus, the lower holiness;
and this is the foundation of the building,
And when he takes the foundation first,
he takes everything, moon and sun.
he merits the aspect of sun and moon,
meaning that he merits the aspect of the moon in its fullness,
and the sun shines upon the moon;
but it does not yet reach the root.
And afterward (in the holy Zohar, ibid.)
דִּבְפֶסַח שֵׁנִי גַּם כֵּן נָטִיל כּוּלָּא
that on Pesach Sheni too one takes everything,
"takes from below to above and does not descend,
it descends from above to below," etc.
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁמּוּבָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
And this accords with what is brought in the holy Zohar
"Your month is in the order of the letters:
the secret of the three, aleph-beis-gimmel," etc.;
"My month is from the end of the letters:
You are from below to above," etc.
And this is the secret of "and I brought you to Me."
And this is what the holy Zohar says:
"this one ascends and does not descend,"
"and I carried you on eagles' wings."
וְזֶהוּ לְמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְפֶסַח רִאשׁוֹן בִּזְמַנּוֹ
And this is for one who merits the first Pesach in its time;
which is not so with Pesach Sheni:
it descends from above to below, like Tishrei,
when one draws down to himself the holiness of Hashem Yisbarach,
וּכְעִנְיַן אֲנִי אֶת דַּכָּא (סוֹטָה ה, א)
like the idea of "I am with the crushed" (Sotah 5a).
And this is the difference: with the first Pesach
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לִבְחִינַת אִישׁ אִישׁ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל
one merits the aspect of "ish ish," as mentioned above;
so that the holiness from above does not rest upon him,
once he has purified and rectified himself
Therefore, on Pesach Sheni, in its eating,
שֶׁאָז הַזְּמַן לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְשׁוּבָה
for then is the time to rectify through teshuvah;
and especially when it falls on Shabbos,
as it is written, "It is good to give thanks to Hashem";
אִיתָא שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁמּוֹדֶה פְּשָׁעָיו וְעוֹזֵב
it is stated that whoever confesses his sins and forsakes them
is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom,
in the manner of what is said,
"One who confesses and forsakes will be shown mercy."
כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה וְכוּלֵּי
"Such is the power of teshuvah," etc.;
'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos,'" etc.
